items.title: How do you apply for jobs in the age of AI?
items.raw_excerpt: With AI being used by applicants to spam-apply to any open positions, and recruiters using AI as a filter, it feels like there's a lot of noise and few humans in the system right now. I thought about simply doing the same (building some n8n automation, or using one of the countless find-a-job-and-apply AI tools on GitHub), but I think there's a better way to do all of this - maybe even by getting around all of this AI shitshow?! Things I was thinking about: - don't optimize the CV/motivational letter with AI so that it sounds authentic - do unsolicited applications at companies i find interesting (since no job posting is open, no AI will suggest this company - and probably the recruiter will read the application) - do more networking (i hate that shit but IK its the most effective)

excerpt_i18n.en: If your impression of AI is still confined to dialog boxes on your phone screen, or just having it draw pictures or write poetry, then at the opening exhibition of China's smart hardware in 2026, a 3D printer at the Creality booth might refresh your perspective. In the 5,000+ square meter exhibition area, Creality's new product, the SPARKX i7, became the star attraction. Many visitors gathered around this small machine that was "creating objects out of thin air" and marveled: I used to think 3D printing was a toy for geeks with a high barrier to entry, but now watching this operation, why does it seem as simple as ordering takeout? This is precisely the message Creality aims to convey with the SPARKX i7: the "iPhone moment" for 3D printing has truly arrived. The SPARKX i7 is intelligent and user-friendly, lowering the barrier to entry. excerpt_i18n.en: Meta's multi-billion dollar acquisition of Manus reflects its confidence in the evolution of "intelligent capability" from "brain-only" to "brain-and-hand" proficiency. IT veteran Li Guoping commented on Manus's change of ownership, noting that the "intelligent capability" refers to the composite ability of intelligent agents (Agents) in both cognition and execution. In his view, the SaaS industry is also undergoing its own intelligent transformation—"If SaaS continues to rely primarily on human-system (interface) interaction without embracing intelligent transformation, it will inevitably be overturned by the times." The fundamental shift in human-computer interaction models represents a disruptive change brought by the Agent wave to the SaaS industry. This assertion stems from Li Guoping's decades of firsthand experience with transformative turning points: during the software era, operating systems were the core of the digital world; in the PC internet era, portals and later search engines became the gateways to the digital world, which shifted to apps in the mobile internet era; and in the cloud computing era, SaaS integrated and encapsulated all capabilities. Li Guoping, who worked at Microsoft for over a decade, currently serves as the Dean of the Digital Economy and Fintech Research Institute at Baiwang Co., Ltd., a leading domestic tax and finance SaaS provider. Over the nearly 20 years since the rise of cloud computing, he has consistently embraced and adopted new technological waves. Where will the future of SaaS head under the Agent wave? On January 7 local time, during the global tech event CES 2026, Mobvoi hosted a new product launch themed "Beyond Recording," officially unveiling the TicNote series—the first 4G AI recording earbuds TicNote Pods, the first AI recording watch TicNote Watch, and the AI-native file collaboration platform TicNote Cloud. Powered by the core engine Shadow AI 2.0, these products form a closed-loop workflow of "recording, documentation, execution, and collaboration," driving TicNote to evolve into a knowledge management and collaboration ecosystem. From expanding hardware forms and iterating on self-developed agents to developing a supporting collaboration platform, these changes mark Mobvoi's commitment to empowering the next stage of organizational collaboration through the TicNote ecosystem.

The launch of the TicNote series redefines the smart experience. As the first AI recording earbuds supporting 4G networks, TicNote Pods do not rely on smartphones, enabling faster upload of recordings to the cloud for AI processing and returning results to users, with a 50% speed increase compared to traditional connection methods. The earbuds are no longer just accessories or extensions of phones but independent AI terminals. Additionally, TicNote Pods support face-to-face translation and simultaneous interpretation, helping users navigate complex language environments with ease and stay focused on the conversation at hand.

Al integrar el motor central Shadow AI 2.0, se forma un ciclo completo de "grabación-documentación-ejecución-colaboración", impulsando a TicNote hacia la gestión del conocimiento.
